evidence.text: Why does adding a negative-curvature alternative change the phenomenological implications of the original gradient conjecture? The reviewed examples are positive stationary potentials, the electroweak Higgs potential, quintessence, and slow-roll inflation.

evidence.text: How can positive late-time energy coexist with the exact-potential restriction? The paper considers a metastable perturbative vacuum and a rolling scalar configuration.

evidence.text: Do familiar low-energy scalar potentials contain positive-energy stationary points incompatible with the original de Sitter proposal? The paper uses the Higgs potential and a conditional axion potential as examples.

evidence.text: Can present acceleration arise from thermal trapping at positive energy even when the underlying zero-temperature potential obeys a de Sitter restriction?

evidence.text: How long may the constructed scalar configuration persist under the earlier constraint invoked by the paper? The appendix compares its residence time with H⁻¹ ln(1/H).

evidence.text: Do ordinary scalar potentials contain positive stationary configurations that defeat universal censorship? Higgs, meson, and axion examples connect this question to particle physics.

evidence.text: The conjecture supplies a proposed quantum-gravity restriction on scalar potentials. The paper asks whether enforcing this slope bound changes the existence or character of singularities in its RS-II dark-energy system.

evidence.text: The baseline asks whether a single scalar in conventional GR can sustain slow roll and the paper's target of 60–70 e-folds while obeying two proposed quantum-gravity bounds.

evidence.text: Stabilize the symmetric sector, identify a light combination, perturb its potential and verify heavy-field shifts and physical scales. This paper applies the procedure to two chiral moduli and a pST deformation.

sources.title: The zoo plot meets the swampland: mutual (in)consistency of single-field inflation, string conjectures, and cosmological data

evidence.text: Compute CMB predictions with CAMB, explore the likelihood with eight CosmoMC Metropolis–Hastings chains, apply R−1<0.05, and extract 68% and 95% probability contours for comparison with theoretical inequalities.

sources.title: The dS swampland conjecture with the electroweak symmetry and QCD chiral symmetry breaking

evidence.text: Solve the sourced scalar's stationarity equation before applying the gradient conjecture. This avoids counting a removable tadpole as an independent gradient, provided the shifted branch exists, is stable and admits a controlled local expansion.

sources.title: Warm inflation as a way out of the swampland

evidence.text: Differentiate the dissipation law at fixed coefficient and exponent, replace temperature perturbations through the bath equation of state, then solve the coupled fluctuation problem. The response function requires that additional dynamics; the algebraic variation only exposes the coupling.

sources.title: Phenomenological Consequences of the Refined Swampland Conjecture

evidence.text: Differentiate the full potential, partition the valid trajectory by curvature, and test the gradient wherever curvature is insufficient. Replace this interval audit by one transition value only after verifying monotonicity and coverage.

sources.title: Notes on quantum corrections of swampland and trans-Planckian censorship conjectures

evidence.text: The reviewed conjectures ask whether a quantum-gravity-compatible effective theory can support a sufficiently flat positive potential or a long period of inflation.
